sanjay: Quick staging run update — enabled speculative decoding (early-prefill) on nova-7b-quant.
Command used:
```
./run_onboard.sh --model nova-7b-q --speculative true --spec-budget 64 --eval-set on-llm-bench-v2
```
Initial numbers: median latency down ~28%, throughput +1.9x, token cost -38% vs non-spec quant. Quality: small but consistent regressions on TriviaQA subset (EM -1.7%) and a bump in hallucination flags on long-form prompts. Raw logs & artifacts uploaded. :eyes:

maria: Nice. What's the sample size and random seed setup for the run? Also which metrics exactly?

sanjay: sample = 2k prompts (mix: QA/chat/long-form) drawn from on-llm-bench v2. We ran 3 seeds (different RNGs) per config. Metrics: EM/F1 (for QA), RougeL (longform), mean logprob delta, and our qual-checker hallucination rate. Quick summary table will follow.

devon: Can we separate quantization vs speculative path effects? I worry the early-token heuristics might bias sampling.

sanjay: Good call. I already kicked off an isolation run: same quant (8-bit PTQ) with speculative=false. Early glance: speculative-off quant baseline shows stable quality vs fp16 baseline; so regressions look tied to speculative prefills rather than quant alone.

kyle: Could be KV-cache staleness or stale attention state when we merge speculative tokens. Remember lazy-kv drift from last month. @eng-runtime any known interactions?

ops-bot: deploy succeeded to staging at 2024-03-02T15:12Z :white_check_mark:

maria: Proposed ablation: run spec-budget in [8,16,32,64], measure EM/F1, halluc rate, and compute divergence metric (KL between token distributions). Also replay logged queries through non-spec pipeline to compute output delta.

sanjay: On it. Also will run deterministic top-k/topp ablations to separate sampling variance.

devon: Add runs with deterministic decoding (top-p=0, temperature=0) so we can measure pure scoring differences vs generative sampling noise.

sanjay: Quick snapshot of the first ablation (single seed):
- spec-budget=8: throughput +1.1x, EM delta -0.1%
- spec-budget=16: throughput +1.4x, EM delta -0.4%
- spec-budget=32: throughput +1.7x, EM delta -0.9%
- spec-budget=64: throughput +1.9x, EM delta -1.7%

maria: That looks like a roughly monotonic tradeoff. Do we have per-prompt breakdown? Are the regressions concentrated on long-context QA or specific templates?

sanjay: Per-prompt diffs suggest most regressions concentrated in long-context multi-hop QA and several prompts with ambiguous clarifying context (speculative tokens sometimes greedily fill clarifiers). I can attach a shortlist of worst offenders.

maria: Could a lightweight reranker after the speculative pass help? E.g., cross-encoder rescoring of top-N continuations.

sanjay: Tried a small reranker (tiny cross-encoder) on top-3 speculative candidates. Results: hallucination rate cut by ~60% for the problematic set, but added ~60ms overhead. Net p95 latency still ~24% better than baseline without spec.

kyle: p95 numbers with/without reranker?

sanjay: baseline p95=420ms; spec64 p95=260ms; spec64 + rerank p95=320ms. Throughput still >1.5x vs baseline.

devon: Nice trade. We should add rerank as opt-in for safety-sensitive routes.

maria: I'll open an eval ticket and mark this as Q-risk=moderate for canary. Also add the replay-based divergence test to the checklist.

sanjay: Dropping reproducible script and logs:
- run script: /mnt/runs/1777003331/run_spec_onboard.sh
- artifacts: /mnt/runs/1777003331/spec_onboard.tar.gz

ops-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-staging/spec-onboard/1777003331/spec_onboard.tar.gz :package:

kyle: Let's schedule 30min sync tomorrow to decide rollout thresholds and whether rerank should be default for longform routes. :calendar:

maria: Agreed. Also propose adding an automated canary gate: if EM drop >1% or hallucination delta >0.5% on holdout, block rollout.

sanjay: Sounds good. I'll post the full CSVs and per-prompt diffs in the ticket once the 8/16/32 runs finish. :rocket:
